NaQSA and/NaMSA could be effective antioxidants in cadmium intoxication and that NaQSA is more effective than NaMSA.
the water-soluble quarcetin-5'- sulfonic acid sodium salt NaQSA and morin- 5'-sulfoncic acid sodium salt NaMSA could exert an antagonisic effect on cadmium toxicity.
the water-soluble quaternary salts of flavonoids quercetin and morin significantly counteracted cadmimum-induced decreases in SODE and GSH levels in mice liver in subacute cadmium toxicity model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possibility of using water-soluble quertin-5'- and morin- 5'-sulfonates to protect liver cells from oxidative stress caused by cadmium.
the influence of water-solubility of flavonoids on the antioxidant properties of these compounds.
the protective effects of water-solubilized quercetin- and morin-sulfonic acids on the antioxidant parameters in the liver of mice exposed to cadmium.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NaQSA and/ or NaMSA could be considered as potential protective agents against cadmium intoxication.
NaQSA and/or NaMSA could be used as effective antioxidants in the treatment of acute and chronic cadmium intoxication.
the tested flavonoids could be considered as a potential therapeutic agent in the subacute intoxication model.
